silo_relevance: This paper is highly relevant to portfolio_optimization because it proposes a concrete portfolio selection and rebalancing method for constructing short-selling portfolios, with an explicit optimization objective, binary asset-selection encoding, and benchmarked performance outcomes across multiple markets. Its main contribution is not just a financial signal, but a full optimization workflow for selecting assets, updating candidate portfolios, and evaluating portfolio-level performance.

key_points.point: The paper formulates portfolio optimization as binary asset selection for short-selling portfolios in G7 markets, making the optimization target directly about portfolio construction rather than single-asset prediction.
key_points.silo_note: This is central to portfolio_optimization because it defines the decision variables, investable universe, and market scope of the optimization problem.

key_points.point: The ELSA-GNQTS procedure provides a portfolio search mechanism with measurement, probability updates, and entanglement-inspired neighborhood moves over asset combinations.
key_points.silo_note: This matters for portfolio_optimization because it is an explicit algorithm for exploring the combinatorial space of portfolio weights/selection states.

key_points.point: The trend ratio is used as the portfolio objective/evaluation criterion and is presented as better aligned with short portfolio design than the Sharpe ratio.
key_points.silo_note: For portfolio_optimization, the choice of objective function is crucial; this paper’s main contribution is a portfolio-level metric tailored to the desired portfolio trajectory.

key_points.point: The reported results show that the constructed portfolios have lower risk and higher trend ratio than single-stock short positions, and outperform Sharpe-ratio-based portfolios on risk, drawdown, profit factor, and trend ratio.
key_points.silo_note: These are directly relevant because they evaluate whether the optimization method improves portfolio-level outcomes relative to simpler portfolio baselines.

key_points.point: The sliding-window rebalancing setup and the note about year-on-year business-cycle effects highlight how portfolio optimization performance depends on the rebalancing horizon and data freshness.
key_points.silo_note: This matters for portfolio_optimization because rebalancing frequency and training-window design are core implementation choices that affect out-of-sample portfolio performance.
